key_features.classic_presentation: Peptic ulcer disease presents with epigastric burning or gnawing pain, often related to meals. Gastric ulcer: pain with eating. Duodenal ulcer: pain 2-3 hours after meals, relieved by eating. May have nausea, early satiety. Chronic/recurrent pattern typical.
key_features.typical_demographics: H. pylori infection and NSAIDs are major risk factors. Can occur at any age but peak 55-65 years. Male slight predominance for duodenal ulcers.
key_features.pathophysiology_brief: Imbalance between gastric acid/pepsin and mucosal defense mechanisms leads to erosion through stomach or duodenal lining.

diagnostic_questions.context: Epigastric location is typical. Pain is midline or slightly off-center.
Burning or gnawing quality is characteristic. Sharp pain suggests perforation.
Gastric ulcer: pain WITH meals. Duodenal ulcer: pain 2-3h AFTER meals, relieved by eating. Night pain (2-3am) classic for duodenal.
NSAIDs are major risk factor (30% of ulcers). Ask about all pain medications.
Peptic ulcers are typically chronic/recurrent, not acute first-time presentation.
Temporary relief with antacids or food is suggestive of peptic ulcer.
Chronic condition with episodic pain over weeks to months.

differential_diagnosis.key_difference: Heartburn, regurgitation, lying down worsens, no meal relationship
More diffuse pain, often acute onset, alcohol/NSAID related
Radiates to back, severe (8-10/10), acute onset

red_flags.finding: Sudden severe pain with rigid abdomen

red_flags.action: Upper GI bleed - emergency care needed
GI bleeding - go to ER immediately

typical_management: PPI therapy (omeprazole, pantoprazole), H. pylori testing and treatment if positive, stop NSAIDs. Most heal with 4-8 weeks of treatment.
disposition: Uncomplicated: outpatient management. Bleeding or perforation: emergency department.
patient_education: Peptic ulcers are sores in the stomach or intestine lining. Treatment includes medications to reduce acid and antibiotics if H. pylori is present. Avoid NSAIDs. Most heal completely with treatment.
